why_it_matters_here: Chemical recovery indicator; the brief's main oil contaminant measure. Without it the tool predicts physical and vegetation recovery but not chemical recovery.
open_source_candidates: Zengel 2015 S1 Table (group means only, 2011-2012, Bay Jimmy; in DER-ZENGEL2015); NCEI 0163796 (ERMA analytical data incl. nearshore sediment tPAH 2010-2011); NOAA DIVER NRDA sample chemistry (public ERDDAP). Coverage of our edge cells unverified.
comment: Group means only (5-9 plots), no plot-level values, so it cannot enter a cell-level model. Weight basis (dry/wet) and depth interval to be checked against the paper before use. Total PAH is not the bioavailable fraction.

why_it_matters_here: Hopane-normalised PAH separates real degradation from dilution or physical removal, and forensic ratios confirm the oil is Macondo. Needed before calling a fall in tPAH 'chemical recovery'.
open_source_candidates: NCEI 0163796 forensic classification layers; DIVER NRDA chemistry (unverified for marsh-edge samples).
comment: Highest-value chemistry addition for the recovery engine; without normalisation a cleanup that removes surface soil looks like 'faster degradation'.

why_it_matters_here: Toxicity to benthos and roots follows freely dissolved PAH, not total; equilibrium-partitioning estimates need organic carbon too.
open_source_candidates: None found in open data for these sites.
comment: Without it, risk can only be ranked by total PAH, which overstates risk in organic-rich marsh soils (strong sorption).

why_it_matters_here: Bulk oil residue; the measure response teams often used for cleanup endpoints.
open_source_candidates: NCEI 0086261 Scribe response databases (TPH among analytes; marsh samples present, coverage unverified).
comment: Method-dependent (GRO/DRO/ORO ranges); must harmonise method before pooling.

why_it_matters_here: Controls PAH sorption and bioavailability, soil strength and erodibility; organic vs mineral marsh soils may respond differently to oiling and to trampling during cleanup.
open_source_candidates: CRMS soil properties (CPRA, per station); Delta-X soil properties (ORNL DAAC, Terrebonne/Atchafalaya 2021); USDA SSURGO map units; a J. Coastal Res. 33(3):507-517 study of CRMS bulk density and organic matter across coastal Louisiana.
comment: Most promising covariate to add for P2-style transfer: CRMS gives station-level values that could be interpolated to edge cells, but CRMS stations sit hundreds of metres from the edge (see event study), so edge soils may differ.

why_it_matters_here: Converts concentrations to mass per area; low-density organic soils erode differently and are more prone to compaction and rutting under mechanical cleanup.
comment: Pair with organic matter; together they distinguish organic from mineral marsh.

why_it_matters_here: Erodibility and oil penetration depth; the process model's 'substrate permeability' input is currently categorical and ASSUMED.
open_source_candidates: SSURGO; CRMS (check whether texture is in the soil deliverables).
comment: Would let the penetration and permeability inputs come from data instead of user choice.

why_it_matters_here: Anaerobic marsh soils slow oil biodegradation; the process model's oxygen limitation uses ASSUMED rates.
open_source_candidates: None found in open data for these sites.
comment: Without Eh, biodegradation-based options (bioremediation, natural attenuation) cannot be screened on soil conditions.

why_it_matters_here: Sulfide stress drives Spartina dieback and interacts with oil stress; relevant to vegetation recovery and planting success.
open_source_candidates: None found in open data for these sites.
comment: Mechanistic covariate for biological recovery; not available at scale.

why_it_matters_here: Plant stress; basins differ in freshwater input (Terrebonne vs Breton/Caernarvon diversion), which may explain part of the between-basin differences in P2.
open_source_candidates: CRMS porewater salinity (discrete, per station; in the CPRA database, not in our derived CRMS file).
comment: Candidate for explaining why the oiling uplift is unstable between basins (P2).

why_it_matters_here: Low priority in flooded marsh; relevant if soils are drained or for acid-sulfate settings elsewhere.
Screening of biostimulation (nutrient addition) depends on existing N and P limitation.
comment: Needed before the tool can rank bioremediation on evidence.

why_it_matters_here: Physical link between oiling, root damage and edge erosion; supports the mechanism behind the edge-loss result.
open_source_candidates: Zengel 2022 GRIIDC sheet 'Shear strength' (SHST_KPA by plot, now in the variable dictionary).
comment: Plot data are in hand but not analysed: by our reading, untreated and mechanical plots are lower than reference and manual in between (n = 4-5 per group, no intervals, sampling date not yet checked). Candidate exploratory analysis; would need its own plan.

why_it_matters_here: Root mortality is the likely pathway from oiling to erosion; would explain rather than only predict edge loss.
open_source_candidates: Zengel et al. papers report some belowground data (not checked); not found as open plot data.
comment: Mechanism, not needed for prediction in the PoC.

why_it_matters_here: Flooding frequency is in the brief; low marsh drowns and erodes differently.
open_source_candidates: CRMS hydrographic and elevation data (per station); coastal DEMs.
comment: Could be added as an exposure covariate in a later P2 rerun.
